lastText: OHLLAGEBERICHTHome1914191519161917191811 November 1918The RequestThe army in the west is not broken in the sense the word is used in staff colleges. It is retreating in order, on ground it still holds, in front of an enemy it can still hurt. What has gone is the possibility of any outcome except a worse one later. The Americans came late and in smaller numbers, and it made a difference of months rather than of outcome. The request goes forward from the Supreme Command. It is a military judgment, made by soldiers, and within a few years a great many people who were in this building will say it was made by someone else.The front · 11 November 1918Expand the mapBerlinKoblenzLuxembourgYpresGorliceVerdunCharlevillePlessKreuznachBad HomburgBrest-LitovskSaint-QuentinAvesnesSoissonsSpa-5MANPOWER ▾-6MUNITIONS ▾+1HOME FRONT ▾Settled recordChief of the General Staff at the close: Hindenburg. The war ends on the eleventh of November. The deployment, August 1914: as the plan was written. Lorraine, August 1914: reinforced. The Marne: delegated forward under plenipotentiary authority. Two corps for the east: kept on the right. Ypres, November 1914: one more concentrated attack. The eastern front, 1915: German divisions in the Carpathians and nothing larger. Serbia: attacked in October 1915. The Meuse: fought as a battle for the fortress. The Somme: ground given where it was dear. The Hindenburg Programme: a smaller programme.
